label: item 1 — /map's top bar shows the map, behind ?glass=1
notes: Wil chose option A -- items 1 and 3 off v2 so v2 stays shippable while he checks them on his phone. THE REVIEW BRANCH IS IMPOSSIBLE HERE: deploy.yml publishes Pages from main/v2 only, with concurrency group 'pages', and Vercel was dropped for the zero-cost requirement (docs/DEVIATIONS.md), so a branch has no live URL. Delivered instead by the means this repo does have: the ?glass=1 query flag, the same pattern phase C3 used for ?striplab=. Off the flag every route is byte-identical, which is what keeps qa:snap a working safety net on the riskiest pages. ITEM 1 SHIPPED BEHIND THE FLAG. The bottom bar already works because it covers document offsets 645-737 and the shell grows into them (E). The top bar covers offsets -107 to 0, above the document, so at scroll 0 nothing can be there by any mechanism -- the only fix is for the page not to be at scroll 0. Mirrors the E pattern exactly, which is the point: shell height += T, the UI layer keeps its original box (height 100% - E - T, margin-top T) so every anchored element holds its screen position, the canvas reaches T above it (top: -T) as it already reaches E below, the camera takes T back as top padding in both fits and in applyPadding, the overviewCamera cache key includes T because the fit is a discrete search, and map.astro lands the page at scroll T with scroll-behavior forced to auto and scrollRestoration manual. T = round(down, min(110px, 100lvh - 100svh), 1px) inside the existing @supports (-webkit-touch-callout) gate: 110 on Wil's phone (measured top bar 107), 0 wherever there are no bars. VERIFIED with T stood at 110px in env()'s place, the technique RUN-STATE records for safe-area insets: shell 954 = viewport 844 + E0 + T110, UI box 844 unchanged, UI margin-top 110px, canvas top -110px and height 954. Off the flag Chromium reports T=0px with shell/UI/canvas all at today's values and scrollY 0. ITEM 3 NOT SHIPPED. /paintings' bottom needs canvas pixels at offsets 645-737, and the stage is position:sticky whose paint does not reach the inset. The two available fixes are both design or structural changes Wil ruled out: growing the stage box changes the 3D camera's aspect and so the corridor's framing, and un-sticking the corridor rewrites that page's scroll mechanic. Raised for his decision rather than guessed at. NOT VERIFIABLE HERE: the bars themselves, and therefore whether the landed scroll reads as Wil wants on the device.
